content:
irene (Support): forwarding ticket from customer (ACME) — they're seeing recurring 429s on a Dedicated reserved pool despite being under commit. Says errors spike after 12:10 UTC and affect only one route. customer supplied curl + response.

irene (Support): customer curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXXXX\" 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-dedicated-1","input":"hello"}'
```
response (sample):
```json
{
  "error": "rate limit exceeded",
  "code": 429
}

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 2500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 30
Redwood-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
```

irene (Support): reserved pool id: rp-4382, account commit reported to us as 2.5k tokens/sec (customer states steady traffic ~2.1k tokens/sec). Customer says 429s started after a deploy on their side but we saw them from our side too. Ticket: INC-5821.

matt (Eng-Platform): thanks. @anya @sam can you take a look? two immediate asks: (1) confirm whether the 429s are being triggered by edge rate limiter or the central quota service, (2) paste any matching request id logs for req_0a1b2c3d. Also what's the smoothing / burst config for rp-4382?

irene (Support): pasted request id above (req_0a1b2c3d) — customer also attached a small reproducer that does a 2500 qps sustained for 45s then drops. They claim it should have been absorbed by the 10s burst allowance.

anya (Dedicated): looking. rp-4382 config snapshot:
```yaml
reserved_pool_id: rp-4382
commit_tokens_per_sec: 2500
burst_window_seconds: 10
burst_multiplier: 1.2  # allows short bursts up to 20% over commit
smoothing_window_seconds: 10
edge_local_bucket_ttl_seconds: 5
```
This is interesting — edge_local_bucket_ttl is 5s here. Central quota service uses 10s reconciliation windows. If edge uses a local token bucket with a 5s TTL and backend reconciles on 10s granularity, they can temporarily allow slightly more tokens than central thinks, which should not cause 429s on the backend, but if rounding or truncated headers occur the backend might believe the central bucket is exhausted and start returning 429s.

sam (SRE): pulled logs for req_0a1b2c3d across the edge fleet and quota service. Findings: at 12:10:12 UTC we see a traffic spike to ~3.0k tokens/sec for 6s from one customer pod (their reproducer). Edge accepted those requests (local bucket had credits) and forwarded to the backend. At 12:10:18 we see the central quota reconciliation for rp-4382 report negative remaining due to a race: two nodes reconciled concurrently and both applied credits because the reconciliation key TTL was short in Redis. There is a race that double-counts consumed tokens in reconciliation under certain timing. That results in central remaining=0 and immediate 429s for subsequent requests until the next refill.

sam (SRE): TL;DR — root cause looks like a reconciliation race between nodes updating the same reserved-pool counters in Redis. The edge/local buckets allowed the short burst, but the reconciliation step ended up double-applying consumption because of non-idempotent update pattern.

matt (Eng-Platform): ok good catch. That explains why customer saw 429s despite being within commit on average. What's scope and rollback risk for a fix? Is this a config mismatch or code bug?

anya (Dedicated): it's a code bug in the reconciliation path. Specifically: the update uses an optimistic read-modify-write without a compare-and-set; when two reconciliation workers race they can both compute new_remaining = old_remaining - consumed and both write. On high traffic bursts this manifests. Edge local buckets + short TTLs mask the issue until a reconciliation step. We should harden to use an atomic Lua script (Redis EVAL) or a WATCH/MULTI CAS.

anya (Dedicated): immediate mitigations:
- bump edge_local_bucket_ttl from 5 -> 12s for rp-4382 to reduce reconciliation frequency overlap (low-risk config change)
- temporarily increase burst_multiplier to 1.4 so short spikes won't hit central as quickly
- enable per-pool reconciliation semaphore to serialize updates for the pool (short term)

irene (Support): customer wants to know if this is their end or our end and whether they'll incur extra charges if we bump their burst.

anya (Dedicated): this is our bug — customer not at fault. If we increase burst_multiplier and keep traffic inside reserved commit + burst, billing doesn't change (still paid via reserved capacity). If we fall back to hosted tier as a mitigation, that will be billed per-token on top of their reserved contract — we should warn them.

matt (Eng-Platform): action items:
- @anya open a patch to make Redis updates atomic (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/XXXXX) — target hotfix branch.
- @sam put a short-term reconciliation semaphore for rp-4382 and bump edge_local_bucket_ttl to 12s for that pool.
- @irene propose to customer: we will apply temporary config changes now and deploy hotfix next week, and we will waive any overage that results from our mitigation.

rate-limiter-bot: created issue RL-2216 for double-write reconciliation race; assigned to @anya. CI job scheduled. :gear:

sam (SRE): scheduled a quick patch on canary tonight (US-west) for the semaphore + ttl bump. Will monitor for 1 hour post-deploy and share metrics. Monitoring queries: tokens_consumed_by_pool, reconciliation_conflicts, 429_rate_by_pool.

irene (Support): communicated plan to customer, they asked for ETA on fix. I told them canary tonight, full rollout after confirmation (~24-48h). They asked for a workaround — suggested they enable hosted-fallback which we can configure for their route. They said they'd prefer to wait for our fix.

matt (Eng-Platform): FYI — we should also add a dashboard alert for reconciliation_conflicts > 0 to catch this earlier. Filing follow-up ticket to product/console.

anya (Dedicated): PR opened and linked in RL-2216. Hotfix changes: atomic Redis EVAL for pool updates + unit tests for concurrent reconciles. Planning a canary deploy after code review.

irene (Support): will update ticket INC-5821 with today's notes and will flag for billing to waive customer overages if any. Closing loop with customer after canary. :thumbsup:

matt (Eng-Platform): thanks team. keep me posted on canary metrics (embedding the queries into the canary runbook).

irene (Support): last message from customer this morning: "thanks, we appreciate quick turnaround — let us know if you need anything from our side.". I will mark this thread as follow-up until canary done.

sam (SRE): canary completed 12:40 UTC — no reconciliation_conflicts observed for the monitored hour, 429s dropped to baseline. Scheduling full rollout at 02:00 UTC tonight.

irene (Support): customer updated that errors stopped after our canary changes. ticket INC-5821 marked resolved from customer side; keeping internal follow-up until full rollout.

matt (Eng-Platform): closing internal loop after rollout. great work.
